translationRepairs: Changle, Prince of Anle, was made Prince of Changchang in Huangxing year 4 and later transferred to Anle.
Changle, Prince of Anle, was made Prince of Jianchang in Huangxing year 4 and later transferred to Anle.
s0002 enfeoffs 建昌王; Jianchang matches 建昌, while Changchang invents a wrong fief reading.
Early in Yanzhang, in a year of great famine, Yanming spent his household wealth to save several dozen guests and support their families as well.
Early in Yanchang, in a year of great famine, Yanming spent his household wealth to save several dozen guests and support their families as well.
s0098 dates the famine 延昌初; Yanchang is the correct era reading, not Yanzhang.
He, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, and his younger brother Prince of Linhuai Yu were among those whose learning and reputation shone across the age.
He, Prince of Zhongshan Xi, and Xi's younger brother Prince of Linhuai Yu were among those whose learning and reputation shone across the age.
及弟臨淮王彧 attaches 弟 to 中山王熙; ‘his’ after ‘He…Xi…’ can misread Yu as Yanming’s brother, so naming Xi as the elder is a real fix.
When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was posthumously titled grand mentor, his princedom left as before, with the temple name Prince Wenzuan.
When the Deposed Emperor came to the throne he was posthumously titled grand mentor, his princedom left as before, with the posthumous name Prince Wenzuan.
諡曰文宣 is a posthumous name (諡), not a temple name (廟號); replacing ‘temple name’ corrects a terminology error.
Because Gaozu had not taken his mother, Lady Chang, according to proper ritual, he did not permit her to be made princess.
Because his mother, Lady Chang, had not been taken as consort according to proper ritual, Gaozu did not permit her to be made princess.
高祖以納不以禮，不許其為妃 makes 納不以禮 the ground for Gaozu’s refusal; Gaozu is not the agent who took Lady Chang, so the proposed passive is required.
